metadata.title: Device Core

props.name: capability
props.remarks: Business capability for establishing baseline execution trust, identity scope, and non‑equivalence for physical and cyber‑physical devices.

props.name: technology-domain
props.remarks: Connected devices, embedded systems, cyber‑physical systems, sensors, actuators, controllers, and autonomous platforms.

props.name: architecture-pattern
props.remarks: Foundational Zero Trust pattern defining what it means for a device to execute instructions under bounded trust.

props.name: data-pattern
props.remarks: Defines device execution trust as data describing eligibility and boundaries, not as authorization or permission.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Authoritative baseline for basic device cybersecurity capabilities.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Guidance for interpreting and applying IoT cybersecurity capabilities across device classes.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Establishes firmware integrity and platform resilience expectations applicable to devices.

metadata.remarks: Device Core defines the baseline conditions under which a device may execute instructions within an environment. This pattern establishes execution boundaries and non‑equivalence only. It does not assert safety, mission suitability, authorization, or regulatory compliance.

components.title: Device Execution Eligibility
components.description: Defines the minimum conditions under which a device is eligible to execute instructions.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Device execution eligibility is explicitly defined and enforceable.

components.title: Device Trust Boundary
components.description: Establishes an explicit trust boundary between a device and its environment.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Device interactions are mediated and explicitly bounded.

components.title: Device Non‑Equivalence Constraints
components.description: Explicitly defines what device execution eligibility does not grant or imply.

implemented-requirements.remarks: Device execution does not imply authorization, safety, correctness, or mission approval.
